\textbf{\emph{Due before our final exam}}\emph{. You must show work
to receive credit. Each problem is worth 4 out of 100 points.}

\textbf{Decide whether each of the following is  statement. If it
is a statement, decide whether or not it is compound.}
\begin{enumerate}[resume]
\item JCSU is a university, and I am a student.\xspace
\item Is Dr\,Ashe an elephant?\xspace
\end{enumerate}
\textbf{Write a negation of each statement.}
\begin{enumerate}[resume]
\item $y\leq5$\xspace
\item Jane lives in the dorm.\xspace
\end{enumerate}
\textbf{Fill in the following truth tables}.
\begin{enumerate}[resume]
\item \hspace{.25cm}

\begin{enumerate}[resume]
\item []%
\begin{tabular}{cc|c}
$p$ & $q$ & $\sim(p\vee q)$\tabularnewline
\hline 
\hline 
T & T & \tabularnewline
\hline 
T & F & \tabularnewline
\hline 
F & T & \tabularnewline
\hline 
F & F & \tabularnewline
\hline 
\end{tabular}\vspace{.25cm}
\end{enumerate}
\end{enumerate}
\textbf{Let $p$ represent a false statement and $q$ represent a
true statement. Find the truth value of each compound statement.}
\begin{enumerate}[resume]
\item $p\vee\sim q$\xspace
\item $\sim(p\vee\sim q)$\xspace
\end{enumerate}
\textbf{Let $p$ represent a true statement, and $q$ and $r$ represent
false statements. Find the truth value of each compound statement.}
\begin{enumerate}[resume]
\item $q\vee\sim r$\xspace
\item $(\sim p\vee q)\wedge\sim r$\xspace
\end{enumerate}
\textbf{Let $p$ be the statement ``$2>y$'', $q$ be statement
``$8\leq6$,'' and $r$ be the statement ``$19\leq19$.'' Find
the truth value of each compound statement.}
\begin{enumerate}[resume]
\item $\sim p\vee\sim r$\xspace
\item $(\sim r\vee q)\vee\sim p$\xspace
\end{enumerate}
\textbf{Let $\ensuremath{A=\{2,4,6,10\}}$, $\ensuremath{B=\{2,10\}}$,
and $\ensuremath{C=\{2,4,6,10\}}$. Decide whether the following are
true or false.}
\begin{enumerate}[resume]
\item $\ensuremath{B\subset A}$\xspace
\item $\ensuremath{A\subseteq B}$\xspace
\end{enumerate}
\textbf{Let $\ensuremath{E=\{a,b,c\}}$.}
\begin{enumerate}[resume]
\item How many subsets does $E$ have? List them.\xspace\xspace
\end{enumerate}
\textbf{Let $\ensuremath{U=\{1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8,9\}}$, $\ensuremath{A=\{2,4,6,8\}}$,
$\ensuremath{B=\{2,3,4,5,6\}}$, and $\ensuremath{C=\{1,2,3,8,9\}}$.
List the members of each set, using set braces.}
\begin{enumerate}[resume]
\item $\ensuremath{A\cup B}$\xspace
\item $\ensuremath{A\cup(B\cap C)}$\xspace
\item $A'\cap B$\xspace
\end{enumerate}
\textbf{Use a Venn diagram to answer the following question.}
\begin{enumerate}[resume]
\item Of the students in your class, 10 have sisters, 15 have brothers,
5 have a brother and a sister, and 7 have neither a brother or a sister.

\begin{enumerate}
\item How many students have a brother or a sister?\xspace\xspace
\end{enumerate}
\begin{enumerate}[resume]
\item How many students are in the class? \xspace\xspace
\end{enumerate}
\end{enumerate}
\textbf{A fair six sided dice is thrown. Find the probability of each
event.}
\begin{enumerate}[resume]
\item Getting a $3$.\xspace
\item Getting a $3$ or $6$.\xspace
\item Not getting a $3$.\xspace
\item Not getting a $3$ or $6$.\xspace
\end{enumerate}
\textbf{A fair coin is tossed three times in a row. Find the probability
of each event. }
\begin{enumerate}[resume]
\item Getting $3$ heads in a row. \xspace
\item Getting at least two tails in a row (equivalently getting $TTH$ or
$TTT$).\xspace
\end{enumerate}
